_12.haxe_doc: The value at row 1, column 2. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_13.haxe_doc: The value at row 1, column 3. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_14.haxe_doc: The value at row 1, column 4. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_21.haxe_doc: The value at row 2, column 1. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_22.haxe_doc: The value at row 2, column 2. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_23.haxe_doc: The value at row 2, column 3. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_24.haxe_doc: The value at row 2, column 4. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_31.haxe_doc: The value at row 3, column 1. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_32.haxe_doc: The value at row 3, column 2. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_33.haxe_doc: The value at row 3, column 3. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_34.haxe_doc: The value at row 3, column 4. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_41.haxe_doc: The value at row 4, column 1. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_42.haxe_doc: The value at row 4, column 2. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_43.haxe_doc: The value at row 4, column 3. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

_44.haxe_doc: The value at row 4, column 4. Matrixes use row vectors: the 4th row holds the translation.

equal.haxe_doc: Tells if all the values are equal to those of `other`.

identity.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to the identity (no transformation).

isIdentity.haxe_doc: Tells if the matrix is exactly the identity.

isIdentityEpsilon.haxe_doc: Tells if the matrix is the identity, within the tolerance `e`.

initRotationX.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a rotation of `a` radians around the X axis.

initRotationY.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a rotation of `a` radians around the Y axis.

initRotationZ.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a rotation of `a` radians around the Z axis.

initTranslation.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a translation.

initScale.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a scale.

initRotationAxis.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a rotation of `angle` radians around the normalized `axis`.

initRotation.haxe_doc: Sets the matrix to a rotation from Euler angles, in radians.

translate.haxe_doc: Appends a translation: it is applied after the current transformation.

scale.haxe_doc: Appends a scale: it is applied after the current transformation.

rotate.haxe_doc: Appends a rotation from Euler angles, in radians.

rotateAxis.haxe_doc: Appends a rotation of `angle` radians around `axis`.

prependTranslation.haxe_doc: Prepends a translation: it is applied before the current transformation.

getScale.haxe_doc: Returns the scale of each axis (the length of the first three rows), all negated if the matrix is mirrored.

prependRotation.haxe_doc: Prepends a rotation from Euler angles, in radians.

prependRotationAxis.haxe_doc: Prepends a rotation of `angle` radians around `axis`.

prependScale.haxe_doc: Prepends a scale: it is applied before the current transformation.

multiply3x3.haxe_doc: Sets `this` to `a * b`, using only the 3x3 rotation and scale part.

multiply3x4.haxe_doc: Sets `this` to `a * b` for affine matrixes (the last column is assumed to be `0, 0, 0, 1`). Faster than `multiply`.

multiply.haxe_doc: Sets `this` to `a * b`: the transformation `a` followed by `b`. `this` can be `a` or `b`.

getInverse.haxe_doc: Returns the inverse of the matrix. @param m An optional matrix to store the result in.

inverse3x4.haxe_doc: Sets `this` to the inverse of the affine matrix `m` (faster than `initInverse`).

initInverse3x3.haxe_doc: Sets `this` to the inverse of the 3x3 part of `m`.

front.haxe_doc: Returns the normalized X axis (first row): the direction the transformation points to.

right.haxe_doc: Returns the normalized Y axis (second row).

up.haxe_doc: Returns the normalized Z axis (third row).

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy.

load.haxe_doc: Copies the values of `m`.

loadValues.haxe_doc: Sets the 16 values from an array, row by row.

getFloats.haxe_doc: Returns the 16 values, row by row.

getDirection.haxe_doc: Returns the direction of the X axis of the rotation, without the scale.

getEulerAngles.haxe_doc: Extracts Euler rotation angles from rotation matrix

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a string representation of the values.

colorHue.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: rotates the hue by `hue` radians.

colorSaturate.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: changes the saturation (`0` keeps it, `-1` makes it grey).

colorContrast.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: changes the contrast (`0` keeps it).

colorLightness.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: adds `lightness` to the color components.

colorGain.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: blends the color towards `color` (`0xRRGGBB`) by `alpha`.

colorBits.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: mixes the channels according to `bits` (bit `i * 3 + j` copies the input channel `i` to the output channel `j`), blended by `blend`.

colorAdd.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: adds the color `c` (`0xRRGGBB`).

colorSet.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: outputs the constant color `c` (`0xRRGGBB`) with the alpha multiplied by `alpha`.

adjustColor.haxe_doc: For color matrixes: applies the hue, saturation, contrast, lightness and gain adjustments of `col`.

toMatrix2D.haxe_doc: Returns the 2D affine part of the matrix as a `h2d.col.Matrix`.

decomposeMatrix.haxe_doc: Extract the rotation from `inMatrix` and stores it as a quaternion inside the [m12,m13,m21,m23] component instead of the rotation being mixed with the scale.

recomposeMatrix.haxe_doc: Inverts the operation of `decomposeMatrix`, giving back a normal transformation matrix from a decomposed one

new.haxe_doc: Creates a matrix. Its values are not initialized: call `identity()` or use `Matrix.I()`.

class.haxe_doc: The implementation of `Matrix`: use `h3d.Matrix` instead.

abstract.haxe_doc:
A 4x4 transformation matrix. Heaps uses row vectors: a point is transformed with `p * M`, the translation is stored in the 4th row (`_41`, `_42`, `_43`), and `a * b` applies `a` then `b`.
```haxe var m = h3d.Matrix.S(2, 2, 2); // scale m.rotate(0, 0, Math.PI / 4); // then rotate around Z m.translate(10, 0, 0); // then translate var p = new h3d.Vector(1, 0, 0).transformed(m); ```

_new.haxe_doc: Creates a matrix. Its values are not initialized: call `identity()` or use `Matrix.I()`.

multiplied.haxe_doc: Returns `this * m` as a new matrix.

L.haxe_doc: Returns a new matrix from 16 values, row by row.

R.haxe_doc: Returns a new rotation matrix from Euler angles, in radians.

lookAtXInline.haxe_doc: Build a rotation Matrix so the X axis will look at the given direction, and the Z axis will be the Up vector ([0,0,1] by default)

lookAtX.haxe_doc: Returns a rotation matrix whose X axis points to `dir` and whose Z axis is up (`up`, by default `0, 0, 1`).

IDENTITY_DECOMPOSED.haxe_doc: The identity in the decomposed format of `decomposeMatrix` (scale and rotation quaternion stored separately).

slerp.haxe_doc: Sets `this` to the spherical linear interpolation between `q1` and `q2`, at `v` from `0` to `1`.

conjugate.haxe_doc: Inverts the rotation (conjugate of a unit quaternion).

pow.haxe_doc: Makes a unit quaternion to the power of the value.

class.haxe_doc:
A quaternion representing a 3D rotation, used for instance by `h3d.scene.Object` to store its rotation. Most methods modify the quaternion in place.
```haxe var q = new h3d.Quat(); q.initRotateAxis(0, 0, 1, Math.PI / 2); // 90 degrees around Z obj.setRotationQuat(q); ```

alwaysSync.haxe_doc: When unset, the object and all its children will not sync() if this root object or one of its parent is culled or not visible. This allows to optimize cpu cost of objects having many children.

applyAnimationTransform.haxe_doc: When an object is loaded, its position scale and rotation will always be set to the default values (0 for position/rotation and 1 for scale). If it's part of a group/scene or if it's animated, then its position/rotation/scale will be stored into the defaultTransform matrix. Calling this function will reset the defaultTransform to null and instead initialize x/y/z/rotation/scale properties. This will not change the actual position of the object but allows you to move the object more freely on your own. Do not use on an object that is currently being animated, since it will set again defaultTransform and apply twice the transformation.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the materials: a linked list of render passes (`Pass`), each with its own render states and shaders.
The main pass is drawn in the pass named by its `Pass.name` (for instance `"default"` or `"alpha"`), other passes (such as `"shadow"` or `"depth"`) are drawn when the renderer renders that pass name.

t.haxe_doc: The big texture containing the area.

du.haxe_doc: The U offset of the area in the big texture.

dv.haxe_doc: The V offset of the area in the big texture.

su.haxe_doc: The U size of the area in the big texture.

sv.haxe_doc: The V size of the area in the big texture.

width.haxe_doc: The width of the area, in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the area, in pixels.

set.haxe_doc: Changes the image of the area. The big texture is rebuilt by its next `BigTexture.done` call.

setAlpha.haxe_doc: Sets an image whose red channel is copied to the alpha channel of the area.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an area. Use `BigTexture.add` instead.

class.haxe_doc: An area of a `BigTexture` holding one image. Its UV coordinates in the big texture are `du + u * su`, `dv + v * sv`.

id.haxe_doc: An identifier of the big texture, given by its user.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the texture and pixels.

add.haxe_doc: Allocates an area for image `t` and returns it, or `null` if there is no space left.

addEmpty.haxe_doc: Allocates an empty area of the given size, or returns `null` if there is no space left.

done.haxe_doc: Loads all the images (asynchronously when possible) and uploads the texture.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty big texture of `size` x `size` pixels. @param bgColor The color (`0xAARRGGBB`) of the free areas.

class.haxe_doc: A texture atlas packing many images in a single square texture, so that objects using different images can be drawn together (used by `h3d.scene.World`). Images are added with `add`, then loaded and uploaded with `done`. Images are reloaded when their file changes.

typedef.haxe_doc: The blend modes of materials, shared with 2D: see `h2d.BlendMode`.

None.haxe_doc: No culling: both sides are drawn.

Back.haxe_doc: The back faces are not drawn (default).

Front.haxe_doc: The front faces are not drawn.

enum.haxe_doc: The faces culled by a pass (see `Pass.culling`).
A blend factor: the value the source (pixel being drawn) or destination (pixel in the target) color is multiplied by before being combined (see `Pass.blend`).

Equal.haxe_doc: Passes if the values are equal.

NotEqual.haxe_doc: Passes if the values are different.

Greater.haxe_doc: Passes if the new value is greater.

GreaterEqual.haxe_doc: Passes if the new value is greater or equal.

Less.haxe_doc: Passes if the new value is lower.

LessEqual.haxe_doc: Passes if the new value is lower or equal.

enum.haxe_doc: A comparison function, used by the depth test (see `Pass.depthTest`) and the stencil test. The test passes when the new value compared to the stored value matches the function.

Replace.haxe_doc: Sets the value to the reference value.

Increment.haxe_doc: Increments the value, clamped to the maximum.

IncrementWrap.haxe_doc: Increments the value, wrapping to 0 after the maximum.

DecrementWrap.haxe_doc: Decrements the value, wrapping to the maximum below 0.

Invert.haxe_doc: Inverts the bits of the value.

enum.haxe_doc: An operation applied to the stencil buffer value (see `Stencil`).

Linear.haxe_doc: Interpolates between the two nearest mip levels (trilinear filtering).

enum.haxe_doc: How the mip levels of a texture are sampled (see `Texture.mipMap`).

AnisotropicNearest.haxe_doc: Anisotropic filtering for surfaces seen at grazing angles, nearest pixel otherwise.

AnisotropicLinear.haxe_doc: Anisotropic filtering for surfaces seen at grazing angles, linear otherwise.

enum.haxe_doc: How the pixels of a texture are interpolated when sampled (see `Texture.filter`).

Clamp.haxe_doc: Uses the pixels of the edge.

Mirror.haxe_doc: Repeats the texture, mirrored every other time.

enum.haxe_doc: How texture coordinates outside of the `[0, 1]` range are handled (see `Texture.wrap`).
How the source and destination colors (multiplied by their blend factors) are combined (see `Pass.blendOp`).

Target.haxe_doc: Allocate a texture that will be used as render target.

Cube.haxe_doc: Allocate a cube texture. Might be restricted to power of two textures only.

MipMapped.haxe_doc: Activates Mip Mapping for this texture. Might not be available for target textures.

ManualMipMapGen.haxe_doc: By default, textures created with MipMapped will have their mipmaps generated when you upload the mipmap level 0. This flag disables this and manually upload mipmaps instead.

IsNPOT.haxe_doc: This is a not power of two texture. Automatically set when having width or height being not power of two.

NoAlloc.haxe_doc: Don't initialy allocate the texture memory.

Dynamic.haxe_doc: Inform that we will often perform upload operations on this texture

AlphaPremultiplied.haxe_doc: Assumes that the color value of the texture is premultiplied by the alpha component.

WasCleared.haxe_doc: Tells if the target texture has been cleared (reserved for internal engine usage).

Loading.haxe_doc: The texture is being currently loaded. Set onLoaded to get event when loading is complete.

Serialize.haxe_doc: Allow texture data serialization when found in a scene (for user generated textures)

IsArray.haxe_doc: Tells if it's a texture array

AsyncLoading.haxe_doc: Allows a DDS texture to be loaded asynchronously (see hxd.res.Image.ASYNC_LOADING)

LazyLoading.haxe_doc: By default, the texture are loaded from images when created. If this flag is enabled, the texture will be loaded from disk when first used.

Writable.haxe_doc: Texture can be written in shaders using RWTexture

enum.haxe_doc: The flags of a `Texture`, given at creation.

typedef.haxe_doc: The pixel format of a texture, see `hxd.PixelFormat`.

defaultKillAlphaThreshold.haxe_doc: The default alpha threshold under which pixels are discarded when `killAlpha` is enabled on a texture shader.

loadingTextureColor.haxe_doc: The color (`0xAARRGGBB`) of the placeholder used by the drivers for textures not loaded yet or disposed.

shadowShader.haxe_doc: The shader receiving the shadows, added to the materials which receive shadows (`h3d.shader.Shadow` by default).

makeVolumeDecal.haxe_doc: Creates the shader of a volume decal of the given bounds. Can be replaced to use another decal shader.

class.haxe_doc: Global defaults of the materials.

create.haxe_doc: Shortcut to create a material for the current renderer setup using the specific diffuse texture.

model.haxe_doc: The model resource the material was loaded from, used to store its properties (see `MaterialDatabase`).

shadows.haxe_doc: Shortcut to set both `castShadows` and `receiveShadows`. Reads `true` only when both are enabled.

castShadows.haxe_doc: Casts shadows: adds a `"shadow"` pass to the material.

receiveShadows.haxe_doc: Receives shadows: adds the shadow shader (`Defaults.shadowShader`) to the main pass.

staticShadows.haxe_doc: Marks the shadow pass as static: it is only drawn when the static shadows are computed (see `Scene.computeStatic`).

textureShader.haxe_doc: The shader applying `texture`, or `null` if there is no texture.

specularShader.haxe_doc: The shader applying `specularTexture`, or `null` if there is none.

texture.haxe_doc: The diffuse (albedo) texture. Setting it adds or removes the texture shader.

specularTexture.haxe_doc: The specular texture. Setting it adds or removes the specular shader.

normalMap.haxe_doc: The normal map texture. Setting it adds or removes the normal map shader (the mesh needs tangents).

color.haxe_doc: The color multiplied with the texture, `(1, 1, 1, 1)` by default.

specularPower.haxe_doc: The specular power: higher values give smaller highlights (forward renderer).

blendMode.haxe_doc: The blend mode of the main pass. It also selects the pass name: `None` draws in `"default"`, `Alpha` in `"alpha"` (sorted back to front) and the additive modes in `"additive"` (without depth write).

getDefaultModelProps.haxe_doc: This is called after a model has been loaded and the material textures setup. It will build the properties for this material, loading them from storage if necessary

getModelData.haxe_doc: Returns the content of the `materials.props` file of the directory of `model` (cached), or an empty object.

loadMatProps.haxe_doc: Returns the saved properties of `material` for `setup`, or `null`. Properties specific to the material model (`name/modelName`) take precedence.

saveMatProps.haxe_doc: Saves the properties of `material` for `setup` in the `materials.props` file (only on platforms with file system access). Properties equal to the defaults are removed.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty database.

class.haxe_doc: Stores the properties of the materials of models in `materials.props` JSON files, one per resource directory, indexed by material setup name and material name. Used by `MaterialSetup` to load and save the material properties edited in Hide.

current.haxe_doc: The active setup. Change it before creating the scenes (see `PbrMaterialSetup.set`).

name.haxe_doc: The setup name, used to store the material properties per setup (see `MaterialDatabase`).

displayName.haxe_doc: An optional name displayed by tools.

createRenderer.haxe_doc: Creates the renderer of a new scene (`h3d.scene.fwd.Renderer` by default).

createLightSystem.haxe_doc: Creates the light system of a new scene (`h3d.scene.fwd.LightSystem` by default).

createMaterial.haxe_doc: Creates a new material of the class used by this setup.

getDefaults.haxe_doc: Returns the default material properties for the given kind of object (for instance `"particles3D"` or `"ui"`).

loadProps.haxe_doc: Converts saved properties to the material properties of this setup.

loadMaterialProps.haxe_doc: Returns the saved properties of `material` for this setup, or `null`.

saveMaterialProps.haxe_doc: Saves the properties of `material` for this setup.

customMeshInit.haxe_doc: Can be used to perform custom mesh initialization such as computing extra buffers when loading it from HSD or displaying it in tools.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a setup with the given name.

class.haxe_doc:
Defines the rendering setup: which renderer, light system and material class are used by the scenes and models.
The active setup is `MaterialSetup.current`, used when a `Scene` is created and when models are loaded. The default setup uses the forward renderer and `Material`; `PbrMaterialSetup` uses the PBR renderer.

bitsToFields.haxe_doc: Decodes the render state bits of a pass into a list of field names and values (debug).

name.haxe_doc: The name of the renderer pass this pass is drawn in, such as `"default"`, `"alpha"`, `"additive"` or `"shadow"`. See `setPassName`.

enableLights.haxe_doc: If `true`, the light system adds the light shaders when drawing this pass.

dynamicParameters.haxe_doc: Inform the pass system that the parameters will be modified in object draw() command, so they will be manually uploaded by calling RenderContext.uploadParams.

isStatic.haxe_doc: Mark the pass as static, this will allow some renderers or shadows to filter it when rendering static/dynamic parts.

culled.haxe_doc: If `true`, the pass is not emitted (the object is not drawn in this pass).

culling.haxe_doc: The faces which are not drawn (`Back` by default).

depthWrite.haxe_doc: Writes the depth of the drawn pixels (`true` by default).

depthClamp.haxe_doc: Clamps the depth to the near and far planes instead of clipping (requires driver support).

depthTest.haxe_doc: The depth test (`Less` by default): pixels failing it are not drawn.

blendSrc.haxe_doc: The blend factor of the source color. See `setBlendMode` for the common presets.

blendDst.haxe_doc: The blend factor of the destination color.

blendAlphaSrc.haxe_doc: The blend factor of the source alpha.

blendAlphaDst.haxe_doc: The blend factor of the destination alpha.

blendOp.haxe_doc: The blend operation of the colors.

blendAlphaOp.haxe_doc: The blend operation of the alpha.

wireframe.haxe_doc: Draws the triangles edges only (requires the `Wireframe` driver feature).

colorMask.haxe_doc: The channels written, as bits: `1` red, `2` green, `4` blue, `8` alpha, repeated every 4 bits for each render target. See `setColorMask`.

layer.haxe_doc: The drawing order of the pass inside its pass name: lower layers are drawn first, before the depth sorting.

stencil.haxe_doc: The stencil settings, or `null` to disable the stencil test.

load.haxe_doc: Copies the name and render states of `p` (not the shaders).

setPassName.haxe_doc: Changes the renderer pass this pass is drawn in.

blend.haxe_doc: Sets the blend factors of the source and destination, for both the colors and the alpha.

setBlendMode.haxe_doc: Sets the blend factors and operations of a common blend mode.

depth.haxe_doc: Sets the depth write, depth test and depth clamp.

setColorMask.haxe_doc: Sets the channels written to the render target.

setColorMaski.haxe_doc: Adds the channels written to the render target `i` when drawing to several targets.

addShader.haxe_doc: Adds a shader to the pass and returns it. Shaders are sorted by priority (see `hxsl.Shader.setPriority`).

addShaderAtIndex.haxe_doc: Can be used for internal usage

removeShader.haxe_doc: Removes a shader from the pass. Returns `true` if it was found.

removeShaders.haxe_doc: Removes all the shaders of class `t` from the pass.

getShader.haxe_doc: Returns the first shader of class `t` of the pass (excluding the shaders of the parent pass), or `null`.

getShaderByName.haxe_doc: Returns the first shader whose name is `name` (excluding the shaders of the parent pass), or `null`.

getShaders.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator on the shaders of the pass (excluding the shaders of the parent pass).

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the pass, with its render states and shaders. @param parent The parent pass of the copy.

abstract.haxe_doc: Where a `PbrMaterial` is drawn in the PBR renderer pipeline.

PBR.haxe_doc: Lit by the deferred PBR lighting (the `"default"` pass, or `"alpha"` / `"additive"` depending on the blend mode).

Forward.haxe_doc: Drawn after the lighting in the `"forward"` pass, lit by the forward light buffer (for transparent objects).

Overlay.haxe_doc: Drawn on top of the final image (`"overlay"` pass), unlit.

Decal.haxe_doc: A volume decal projecting its textures on the G-buffer (`"decal"` or `"emissiveDecal"` pass).

BeforeTonemapping.haxe_doc: Unlit, drawn in HDR just before tone mapping (`"beforeTonemapping"` pass).

AfterTonemapping.haxe_doc: Unlit, drawn after tone mapping (`"afterTonemapping"` pass).

Distortion.haxe_doc: Drawn in the `"distortion"` pass, used by distortion effects, without depth write.

DecalPass.haxe_doc: Drawn in the decal pass with the material own geometry (no volume projection).

TerrainPass.haxe_doc: Drawn in the `"terrain"` pass, before the other opaque objects.

PBR.haxe_doc: Lit by the deferred PBR lighting (the `"default"` pass, or `"alpha"` / `"additive"` depending on the blend mode).

Forward.haxe_doc: Drawn after the lighting in the `"forward"` pass, lit by the forward light buffer (for transparent objects).

Overlay.haxe_doc: Drawn on top of the final image (`"overlay"` pass), unlit.

Decal.haxe_doc: A volume decal projecting its textures on the G-buffer (`"decal"` or `"emissiveDecal"` pass).

BeforeTonemapping.haxe_doc: Unlit, drawn in HDR just before tone mapping (`"beforeTonemapping"` pass).

AfterTonemapping.haxe_doc: Unlit, drawn after tone mapping (`"afterTonemapping"` pass).

Distortion.haxe_doc: Drawn in the `"distortion"` pass, used by distortion effects, without depth write.

DecalPass.haxe_doc: Drawn in the decal pass with the material own geometry (no volume projection).

TerrainPass.haxe_doc: Drawn in the `"terrain"` pass, before the other opaque objects.

abstract.haxe_doc: The blend mode of a `PbrMaterial` (see `h3d.mat.BlendMode`).
The depth test of a `PbrMaterial` (see `h3d.mat.Data.Compare`).
The depth write of a `PbrMaterial`: `Default` writes depth only for opaque blend modes.
A stencil operation of a `PbrMaterial` (see `h3d.mat.Data.StencilOp`).
A stencil test of a `PbrMaterial` (see `h3d.mat.Data.Compare`).
The face culling of a `PbrMaterial` (see `h3d.mat.Data.Face`).

mode.haxe_doc: Where the material is drawn in the pipeline.

colorMask.haxe_doc: The channels written: bits 0 to 3 for red, green, blue and alpha.

alphaKill.haxe_doc: Discards the pixels whose texture alpha is below the threshold.

parallax.haxe_doc: If positive, enables parallax mapping with this depth, using the alpha channel of `specularTexture` as height.

parallaxSteps.haxe_doc: The number of layers used by the parallax mapping.

invertBasis.haxe_doc: Inverts the tangent basis of the parallax mapping.

textureWrap.haxe_doc: Repeats the textures (`Repeat` wrap mode) instead of clamping them.

enableStencil.haxe_doc: Enables the stencil test and operations below.

stencilPassOp.haxe_doc: The stencil operation when both the stencil and depth tests pass.

stencilFailOp.haxe_doc: The stencil operation when the stencil test fails.

depthFailOp.haxe_doc: The stencil operation when the stencil test passes but the depth test fails.

name.haxe_doc: An optional display name of the properties.

drawOrder.haxe_doc: If set, the pass `layer` (an integer as string): objects of a lower layer are drawn first.

depthPrepass.haxe_doc: Adds a `"depthPrepass"` pass writing the depth before the main pass (for transparent objects needing correct sorting).

flipBackFaceNormal.haxe_doc: Flips the normal of back faces, for double sided materials.

ignoreCollide.haxe_doc: The geometry using this material is excluded from the collision data built by the model converter (`hxd.fs.Convert`).

class.haxe_doc: The properties of a `PbrMaterial`, stored as `props` and edited in Hide. Call `refreshProps()` after changing them.
The material of the PBR renderer (`MaterialSetup` `PbrMaterialSetup`). Its settings are given by its `PbrProps` (usually loaded from the `materials.props` of the model, see `MaterialDatabase`).

set.haxe_doc: Sets a `PbrMaterialSetup` as `MaterialSetup.current`.

gloss.haxe_doc: Tells that this setup uses glossiness. Always `true`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the setup. `name` is used to store the material properties (see `MaterialDatabase`).

class.haxe_doc:
The material setup of the physically based rendering: it creates `PbrMaterial` materials, the `h3d.scene.pbr.Renderer` renderer and the `h3d.scene.pbr.LightSystem`.
Call `set()` before creating the scene (for instance in the `main` function, before creating the `hxd.App`). On WebGL 1, the default renderer is used instead.

readMask.haxe_doc: The bits of the stencil value and reference compared by the test.

writeMask.haxe_doc: The bits of the stencil buffer which can be modified.

reference.haxe_doc: The reference value used by the test and the `Replace` operation.

frontTest.haxe_doc: The stencil test of front faces.

frontPass.haxe_doc: The operation on front faces when both the stencil and depth tests pass.

frontSTfail.haxe_doc: The operation on front faces when the stencil test fails.

frontDPfail.haxe_doc: The operation on front faces when the stencil test passes but the depth test fails.

backTest.haxe_doc: The stencil test of back faces.

backPass.haxe_doc: The operation on back faces when both the stencil and depth tests pass.

backSTfail.haxe_doc: The operation on back faces when the stencil test fails.

backDPfail.haxe_doc: The operation on back faces when the stencil test passes but the depth test fails.

setBack.haxe_doc: Sets the operations of back faces. See `setFront`.

setOp.haxe_doc: Sets the operations of both front and back faces. See `setFront`.

setFunc.haxe_doc: Sets the stencil test of both front and back faces, with its reference value and masks.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the settings.

load.haxe_doc: Copies the settings of `s`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates stencil settings which always pass and keep the stencil buffer unchanged.

enum.haxe_doc: The pixel formats of textures and `Pixels`: color formats (8 bits, half and full floats per channel), compressed formats (`S3TC`, `ASTC`, `ETC`...) and depth formats.

TRILINEAR_FILTERING_ENABLED.haxe_doc: If `true`, mipmapped textures are created with `Linear` mip filtering, otherwise `Nearest`.

DEFAULT_WRAP.haxe_doc: The wrap mode of new textures.

getDefaultDepth.haxe_doc: This will return the default depth buffer, which is automatically resized to the screen size.

fromBitmap.haxe_doc: Creates a texture from a bitmap.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Creates a texture from pixels. @param format The texture format (the pixels format by default).

fromColor.haxe_doc: Creates a 1x1 texture using the RGB color passed as parameter.

genDisc.haxe_doc: Returns a shared `size` x `size` texture with a filled disc of the given color (`0xRRGGBB`).

defaultCubeTexture.haxe_doc: Returns a default dummy 1x1 black cube texture

genChecker.haxe_doc: Returns a checker texture of size x size, than can be repeated

genNoise.haxe_doc: Returns a shared `size` x `size` texture filled with random values.

id.haxe_doc: A unique identifier of the texture.

name.haxe_doc: The texture name (usually its resource path), used for debugging. See `setName`.

width.haxe_doc: The width, in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height, in pixels.

flags.haxe_doc: The flags given at creation, and some state flags such as `Loading`.

mipMap.haxe_doc: How the mip levels are sampled (`None` unless the texture is `MipMapped`).

filter.haxe_doc: How the pixels are interpolated (`Linear` by default).

wrap.haxe_doc: How the texture coordinates outside of `[0, 1]` are handled (`DEFAULT_WRAP` by default).

slice.haxe_doc: For texture arrays: if positive, binds only the layer `slice - 1` as a 2D texture (DirectX 12).

layerCount.haxe_doc: The number of layers: 6 for cube textures, the number of layers of texture arrays, the depth of 3D textures, 1 otherwise.

lodBias.haxe_doc: A bias added to the mip level selected when sampling, from -15 to 16: positive values select less detailed levels.

mipLevels.haxe_doc: The number of mip levels (1 if the texture is not `MipMapped`).

anisotropicMaxLevel.haxe_doc: The maximum level of anisotropic filtering (1 to 16).

startingMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level sampled: levels before it are ignored.

residentMip.haxe_doc: The most detailed mip level allocated on the GPU : mip levels before it are not allocated, and the texture is sampled starting at this level.

isPlaceholder.haxe_doc: A 1x1 texture is allocated while the texture is loading (see hxd.res.Image)

realloc.haxe_doc: If this callback is set, the texture can be re-allocated when the 3D context has been lost or when it's been free because of lack of memory.

depthBuffer.haxe_doc: When the texture is used as render target, tells which depth buffer will be used. If set to null, depth testing is disabled.

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocates the GPU memory of the texture if it is not allocated.

isSRGB.haxe_doc: Tells if the format stores sRGB colors.

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a GPU copy of the texture (same size, format and main flags).

preventAutoDispose.haxe_doc: In case we run out of GPU memory, textures that hasn't been used for a long time will be disposed. Calling this will make this texture not considered for auto disposal.

waitLoad.haxe_doc: Some textures might take some time to load. You can check flags.has(Loading) or add a waitLoad callback which will get called either immediately if the texture is already loaded or when loading is complete.

setName.haxe_doc: Sets the texture name, used for debugging.

isDisposed.haxe_doc: Tells if the GPU memory is released and cannot be restored with `realloc`.

resize.haxe_doc: Changes the texture size. The content is lost.

clearF.haxe_doc: Fills a render target with the given float color. @param layer The layer to clear, or `-1` for all layers.

setResidentMip.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU memory of the mip levels more detailed than `mip` (texture streaming). Returns `false` if the driver does not support it. Not supported for render targets and depth textures.

uploadBitmap.haxe_doc: Uploads the pixels of a bitmap to a mip level and layer. The size must match the mip level size.

uploadPixels.haxe_doc: Uploads pixels to a mip level and layer. The size must match the mip level size. Uploading the level 0 of the last layer of a `MipMapped` texture generates the mip levels, unless `ManualMipMapGen` is set.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU memory of the texture.

hasStencil.haxe_doc: Tells if the format is a depth format with a stencil.

isDepth.haxe_doc: Tells if the format is a depth format.

getHandle.haxe_doc: Returns the bindless handle of the texture (requires a driver supporting bindless textures).

capturePixels.haxe_doc: Downloads the current texture data from the GPU. Beware, this is a very slow operation that shouldn't be done during rendering.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a 3D texture of `w` x `h` x `d` pixels.

class.haxe_doc: A 3D (volume) texture of `width` x `height` x `depth` pixels.

defaultArrayTexture.haxe_doc: Returns a shared 1x1 texture array with a single dark grey layer, used when a texture array is missing.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a texture array of `layers` layers of `w` x `h` pixels.

class.haxe_doc: A texture array: several 2D textures (layers) of the same size and format, sampled with a layer index in shaders.

allowAsync.haxe_doc: If `true`, the images are loaded asynchronously when their format allows it.

setResource.haxe_doc: Fills the channel `c` with the channel `srcChannel` (by default the same) of image `res`, which must have the same size. The channel is updated when the image file changes.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a texture of `w` x `h` pixels with empty channels.

class.haxe_doc: A texture whose channels (red, green, blue, alpha) are filled separately from different images, for instance to pack the roughness, metalness and occlusion maps in a single texture.

texture.haxe_doc: The texture referenced by the handle.

class.haxe_doc: A bindless handle of a texture: an identifier allowing shaders to access the texture without binding it. Requires a driver supporting bindless textures. Created by the driver.

generate.haxe_doc: Generates a `texRes`^3 3D texture (`R8` format) where each pixel stores the distance to the nearest of a set of random points (one per cell of a `gridSize`^3 grid), computed on the CPU. The noise tiles in all directions.

generateOctave.haxe_doc: Generates a `size`^3 3D texture combining `octaves` Worley noises of increasing frequency, starting with `gridSize` cells.

class.haxe_doc: Generates tiling 3D Worley (cellular) noise textures, used for instance for volumetric clouds or fog.
Combines the Worley noise octaves on the GPU (used by `WorleyNoise.generateOctave`).

collidePart.haxe_doc: Tells if the particle `p` collides, and if so stores the surface normal in `normal`.

class.haxe_doc: A collision handler for the particles of an `Emitter` (see `Emitter.collider` and `State.collide`).

VPoly.haxe_doc: A polynomial of coefficients `values` (from degree 0); `points` are the control points it was computed from (for editors).

DEFAULT_RESOLVER.haxe_doc:
This value can be set to use custom type resolvers.
A type resolver finds a `Class` or `Enum` instance from a given `String`. By default, the Haxe `Type` Api is used.
A type resolver must provide two methods:
1. `resolveClass(name:String):Class<Dynamic>` is called to determine a `Class` from a class name 2. `resolveEnum(name:String):Enum<Dynamic>` is called to determine an `Enum` from an enum name
This value is applied when a new `Unserializer` instance is created. Changing it afterwards has no effect on previously created instances.

run.haxe_doc:
Unserializes `v` and returns the according value.
This is a convenience function for creating a new instance of Unserializer with `v` as buffer and calling its `unserialize()` method once.

unserialize.haxe_doc:
Unserializes the next part of `this` Unserializer instance and returns the according value.
This function may call `this.resolver.resolveClass` to determine a Class from a String, and `this.resolver.resolveEnum` to determine an Enum from a String.
If `this` Unserializer instance contains no more or invalid data, an exception is thrown.
This operation may fail on structurally valid data if a type cannot be resolved or if a field cannot be set. This can happen when unserializing Strings that were serialized on a different Haxe target, in which the serialization side has to make sure not to include platform-specific data.
Classes are created from `Type.createEmptyInstance`, which means their constructors are not called.

new.haxe_doc:
Creates a new Unserializer instance, with its internal buffer initialized to `buf`.
This does not parse `buf` immediately. It is parsed only when calls to `this.unserialize` are made.
Each Unserializer instance maintains its own cache.

class.haxe_doc:
The `Unserializer` class is the complement to the `Serializer` class. It parses a serialization `String` and creates objects from the contained data.
This class can be used in two ways:
- create a `new Unserializer()` instance with a given serialization String, then call its `unserialize()` method until all values are extracted - call `Unserializer.run()` to unserialize a single value from a given String
The specification of the serialization format can be found here: <https://haxe.org/manual/serialization/format>

addSub.haxe_doc: Adds a buffer to the primitive, with custom position,scale,rotation. The buffer can have more stride than the BigPrimitive, but not less. It is assumed that the buffer contains [X,Y,Z,NX,NY,NZ,U,V,R,G,B] (depending on his stride) so the different offsets are applied to the corresponding components. If hasTangent=true, we have [TX,TY,TZ] just after normal. However if the stride is 5, we assume [X,Y,Z,U,V] If mat is not null, it overrides dx, dy, dz, rotation, scale

get.haxe_doc: Returns the shared instance.

class.haxe_doc: A full screen quad (two triangles covering clip space from -1 to 1), used to draw screen passes (see `h3d.pass.ScreenFx`).

typedef.haxe_doc: A level of detail of a `Polygon`.

onContextLost.haxe_doc: If set, called to get the data again when the GPU buffers must be reallocated.

class.haxe_doc: A primitive created from raw vertex data (and optional indexes) in any buffer format.

class.haxe_doc: A UV sphere centered on the origin, made of `segsW` meridians and `segsH` parallels.
Shader applying the animated transform of the source object to all the instances of an `AnimMeshBatch`.

shadersChanged.haxe_doc: Set if shader list or shader constants has changed, before calling begin()

instanceCount.haxe_doc: The number of instances on this batch

worldPosition.haxe_doc: * If set, use this position in emitInstance() instead MeshBatch absolute position

primitiveSubMeshes.haxe_doc: Tells the mesh batch to draw only a subpart of the primitive.

curSubMesh.haxe_doc: The index in `primitiveSubMeshes` of the sub mesh drawn by the next `emitInstance`.

cpuIndirectCallBuffers.haxe_doc: Use one indirect call buffer per material. Instances can not be culled for a specific pass yet.

calcBounds.haxe_doc: If set, exact bounds will be recalculated during emitInstance (default true)

curLod.haxe_doc: With EnableCpuLod, set the lod of the next emitInstance. Without EnableCpuLod and not using primitiveSubMeshes, set the lod of the whole batch.

enableStorageBuffer.haxe_doc: * Buffer of per instance params such as position is created as a storage buffer * allowing for huge amount of instances.

enableGpuUpdate.haxe_doc: * Buffer of per instance params such as position is created with its own format * allowing compute shaders to update those parameters.

forceGpuUpdate.haxe_doc: * Force PerInstance to be setup by a compute shader. * Don't support without Storage Buffer to simplify implementation.

enableSubMesh.haxe_doc: * Use sub mesh to emit instance. * Don't support multiple materials without Storage Buffer to simplify implementation.

enablePerInstanceTexture.haxe_doc: * Enable per instance texture if bindless is supported.

enableCpuLod.haxe_doc: Selects the level of detail of each instance on the CPU, according to its screen size (or `curLod` if set). Has no effect if the primitive has a single level of detail. Enables the storage buffer.

emitInstance.haxe_doc: Adds an instance using the current transform of the batch (or `worldPosition` if set) and the current values of the parameters of its shaders.

flush.haxe_doc: Uploads the emitted instances to the GPU. Called automatically during sync.

disposeBuffers.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU buffers of the instances. They are reallocated by the next `flush`.

class.haxe_doc: h3d.scene.MeshBatch allows to draw multiple meshed in a single draw call. See samples/MeshBatch.hx for an example.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a batch of `primitive` whose instances copy the animated local transform of `copyObject`.

class.haxe_doc: A `MeshBatch` whose instances all follow the animated transform of a source mesh (see `AnimMeshBatcher`).

Draws many copies of an animated object with instancing: one `MeshBatch` is created per mesh of the object, and all the copies play the same animation in sync.
Only the transform of each mesh is animated (rigid animations): skeletal deformation is not supported.

ManualEmitGPU.haxe_doc: The compute passes building the draw commands are not run automatically: call `Batcher.syncGPU` and `Batcher.emitGPU` yourself.

enum.haxe_doc: Options of a `Batcher`.

meshes.haxe_doc: The meshes of the model, with their transform relative to the model root.

draws.haxe_doc: The draw passes of the materials.

class.haxe_doc: A model registered in a `Batcher` with `Batcher.addInstance`, which can then be emitted many times.

addModel.haxe_doc: Adds the geometry of a model to the library.

addPolygon.haxe_doc: Adds the geometry of a polygon to the library.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the GPU resources of the library.

checkOffsetBuffer.haxe_doc: Makes sure the per instance index buffer can hold `instanceCount` instances.

class.haxe_doc: The geometry storage shared by `Batcher` instances: the models are packed in one big primitive per vertex format. Share a library between several batchers drawing the same models to avoid duplicating the geometry.

emitInstance.haxe_doc: Adds an instance of `obj` to this group. See `Batcher.emitInstance`.

reserveInstances.haxe_doc: Preallocates `count` instances of `obj` in this group. See `Batcher.reserveInstances`.

remove.haxe_doc: Removes all the instances of this group and releases it.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a group. Use `Batcher.createGroup` instead.

class.haxe_doc: A group of instances of a `Batcher` which can be removed together. Created with `Batcher.createGroup`.

shadowMaxDistance.haxe_doc: If positive, instances farther than this distance are not drawn in the shadow passes.

shadowCameraFrustumCulling.haxe_doc: If `true`, the shadow passes only draw the instances inside the camera frustum (aggressive culling, faster but shadows of objects outside the view can disappear). Otherwise they draw the instances inside the area seen by the camera, extended towards the light by `shadowCullingOffset`.

shadowCullingOffset.haxe_doc: The distance the shadow casting area is extended towards the light, so that objects outside the view still cast shadows inside it.

hzbCulling.haxe_doc: Enables GPU occlusion culling using the hierarchical depth buffer built by the renderer (`RenderContext.hzb`).

isRelative.haxe_doc: If `true`, the instance positions are relative to the batcher transform, so the batcher can be moved. Otherwise they are in world space.

syncShader.haxe_doc: An optional compute shader updating the instance transforms on the GPU each frame (see `BaseSync`), run by `syncGPU`.

hasSyncIDs.haxe_doc: Tells if the `syncShader` uses per instance sync IDs.

addShader.haxe_doc: Adds a shader to all the instances. @param pass The name of the material pass to add the shader to, or `""` for the main pass of every material.

createGroup.haxe_doc: Creates a group of instances, which can be removed together with `BatchGroup.remove`.

reserveInstances.haxe_doc: Preallocates `count` instances of `instance` before emitting them, to avoid reallocations.

syncGPU.haxe_doc: With the `ManualEmitGPU` flag: runs the `syncShader` on all the instances.

emitGPU.haxe_doc: With the `ManualEmitGPU` flag: runs the compute passes culling the instances and building the draw commands.

dump.haxe_doc: Writes a text report of the primitives, models and instances of the batcher to the file `path` (debug).

class.haxe_doc:
A GPU driven renderer for very large numbers of static instances of many different models.
Register each model once with `addInstance`, then add as many instances as needed with `emitInstance`. Instances are kept from frame to frame: they stay until their group is removed (see `createGroup`). The culling (frustum, distance and optionally occlusion with `hzbCulling`) and the level of detail selection are done on the GPU by compute shaders, and the instances are drawn with indirect draw calls, with all the meshes of the same vertex format in a single primitive.
Requires a driver supporting bindless resources (throws otherwise).

Base class of the compute shaders updating the instance transforms on the GPU (see `Batcher.syncShader`). It provides `getModelView` and `fillModelView` to read and write the transform of an instance.

instanceStride.haxe_doc: The number of 4-floats vectors per instance in `instancesData`.

modelViewOffset.haxe_doc: The offset of the transform matrix in the data of an instance.

syncIDs.haxe_doc: The sync IDs of the instances, given to `Batcher.emitInstance`.

hasSyncIDs.haxe_doc: Tells if the shader uses the sync IDs.

class.haxe_doc: The parameters of a `Batcher.syncShader`, filled by the batcher before running it. Implemented by shaders extending `BaseSync`.

is3D.haxe_doc: Setting is3D to true will switch from a screen space line (constant size whatever the distance) to a world space line

clear.haxe_doc: Removes all the lines drawn so far.

setColorF.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the next lines with float components, from `0` to `1`.

drawLine.haxe_doc: Draws a single line from `p1` to `p2`.

moveTo.haxe_doc: Moves the pen to the given local position without drawing. With `is3D`, it also ends the current polyline.

lineTo.haxe_doc: Draws a line from the pen position to the given local position, and moves the pen there.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty graphics object.

color.haxe_doc: The line color, in `0xRRGGBB` format. Changes are applied the next time the bounds change.

bounds.haxe_doc: The box bounds, in local space. If `null`, a unit box centered on the origin (from -0.5 to 0.5) is drawn.

thickness.haxe_doc: The line thickness. Changes are applied the next time the bounds change.

class.haxe_doc:
A debug wireframe box, drawn with 12 lines.
The lines are rebuilt automatically during sync whenever `bounds` changes. It has no collider and is meant for visualizing bounds; use `h3d.prim.Cube` with a `Mesh` for a solid box.

getCameraControllersClass.haxe_doc: Returns the available controller classes (used by editors to let the user pick one).

getCameraControllerClassIdx.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the class of `ctrl` in `getCameraControllersClass()`, or `-1`.

distance.haxe_doc: The current distance between the camera and its target.

targetDistance.haxe_doc: The distance the camera is moving to.

theta.haxe_doc: The current horizontal angle of the camera around the target, in radians.

phi.haxe_doc: The current vertical angle of the camera, in radians, from `0` (looking down from above) to `PI` (looking up from below).

fovY.haxe_doc: The current vertical field of view, in degrees.

target.haxe_doc: The current position the camera is looking at.

minDistance.haxe_doc: The minimum distance reachable by zooming.

maxDistance.haxe_doc: The maximum distance reachable by zooming.

enableZoom.haxe_doc: If `true`, the mouse wheel changes the distance to the target. Otherwise it moves the camera forward and backward.

zoomAmount.haxe_doc: The distance multiplier applied for each mouse wheel step.

friction.haxe_doc: The inertia damping of rotations, between `0` (rotation keeps going) and `1` (stops immediately).

smooth.haxe_doc: The smoothing of the camera movement, between `0` (immediate) and `1` (never reaches the target).

lockZPlanes.haxe_doc: If `false`, the camera `zNear` and `zFar` are adjusted to the distance to the target.

wantedFOV.haxe_doc: The vertical field of view, in degrees, applied by `OrbitCameraController` and `FPSCameraController` every frame.

moveSpeed.haxe_doc: The speed of the keyboard movements.

set.haxe_doc: Set the controller parameters. Distance is ray distance from target. Theta and Phi are the two spherical angles Target is the target position

loadFromCamera.haxe_doc: Load current position from current camera position and target. Call if you want to modify manually the camera.

initFromScene.haxe_doc: Initialize to look at the whole scene, based on reported scene bounds.

toTarget.haxe_doc: Stop animation by directly moving to end position. Call after set() if you don't want to animate the change

onCustomEvent.haxe_doc: Called for each scene event before the controller handles it. Set `e.propagate = false` to prevent the controller from handling the event.

onClick.haxe_doc: Called when the user clicks (presses and releases quickly without moving) with the button used to move the camera.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a controller. It must be added to the scene (directly or through `parent`) to control its camera. @param distance The initial distance to the target.

class.haxe_doc:
Base class of the mouse/keyboard camera controllers. Add a controller to the scene to drive `Scene.camera`: it listens to the scene events and moves the camera smoothly towards the wanted position every frame.
The camera position is expressed in spherical coordinates around `target`: `distance`, `theta` (horizontal angle) and `phi` (vertical angle, from the Z axis). Use `set` to change them and `loadFromCamera` to start from the current camera. See `OrbitCameraController` and `FPSCameraController`.

zNear.haxe_doc: The camera near plane distance, applied every frame.

zFar.haxe_doc: The camera far plane distance, applied every frame.

color.haxe_doc: The line color, in `0xRRGGBB` format. Changes are applied the next time `radius` or `length` is set.

radius.haxe_doc: The capsule radius. Setting it redraws the lines.

length.haxe_doc: The length of the cylindrical part along the X axis, excluding the caps. Setting it redraws the lines.

class.haxe_doc:
A debug wireframe capsule aligned on the X axis: a cylinder of `length` capped by two half spheres of `radius`.
It has no collider and is meant for visualizing capsule colliders (see `h3d.col.Capsule`).
