remove.haxe_doc:
Removes all `name` metadata entries from the origin of `this` MetaAccess.
This method might clear several metadata entries of the same name.
If a `Metadata` array is obtained through a call to `get`, a subsequent call to `remove` has no effect on that array.
If `name` is null, compilation fails with an error.

has.haxe_doc:
Tells if the origin of `this` MetaAccess has a `name` metadata entry.
If `name` is null, compilation fails with an error.

get.haxe_doc:
Return the wrapped `Metadata` array.
Modifying this array has no effect on the origin of `this` MetaAccess. The `add` and `remove` methods can be used for that.

extract.haxe_doc:
Extract metadata entries by given `name`.
If there's no metadata with such name, empty array `[]` is returned.
If `name` is null, compilation fails with an error.

add.haxe_doc:
Adds the metadata specified by `name`, `params` and `pos` to the origin of `this` MetaAccess.
Metadata names are not unique during compilation, so this method never overwrites a previous metadata.
If a `Metadata` array is obtained through a call to `get`, a subsequent call to `add` has no effect on that array.
If any argument is null, compilation fails with an error.

typedef.haxe_doc: MetaAccess is a wrapper for the `Metadata` array. It can be used to add metadata to and remove metadata from its origin.

grow.haxe_doc: Makes the buffer at least `v` indexes long, filling with zeros.

resize.haxe_doc: Changes the length to `v`, truncating or filling with zeros.

iterator.haxe_doc: Returns an iterator on the indexes.

QWERTY_EQUALS.haxe_doc: The key of the `=` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_MINUS.haxe_doc: The key of the `-` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_TILDE.haxe_doc: The key of the ``` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_BRACKET_LEFT.haxe_doc: The key of the `[` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_BRACKET_RIGHT.haxe_doc: The key of the `]` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_SEMICOLON.haxe_doc: The key of the `;` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_QUOTE.haxe_doc: The key of the `'` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_BACKSLASH.haxe_doc: The key of the `\` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_COMMA.haxe_doc: The key of the `,` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_PERIOD.haxe_doc: The key of the `.` character on QWERTY keyboards.

QWERTY_SLASH.haxe_doc: The key of the `/` character on QWERTY keyboards.

INTL_BACKSLASH.haxe_doc: The backslash key next to the left Shift on some keyboards. Not available on SDL.

AZERTY_DOLLAR.haxe_doc: The key of the `$` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_EQUALS.haxe_doc: The key of the `=` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_COMMA.haxe_doc: The key of the `,` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_SEMICOLON.haxe_doc: The key of the `;` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_COLON.haxe_doc: The key of the `:` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_MODULO.haxe_doc: The key of the `ù` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_PARENT_CLOSE.haxe_doc: The key of the `)` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_MULTIPLY.haxe_doc: The key of the `*` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_POWER.haxe_doc: The key of the `^` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_SQUARED.haxe_doc: The key of the `²` character on AZERTY keyboards.

AZERTY_EXCLAM.haxe_doc: The key of the `!` character on AZERTY keyboards.

NUMBER_0.haxe_doc: The 0 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_1.haxe_doc: The 1 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_2.haxe_doc: The 2 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_3.haxe_doc: The 3 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_4.haxe_doc: The 4 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_5.haxe_doc: The 5 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_6.haxe_doc: The 6 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_7.haxe_doc: The 7 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_8.haxe_doc: The 8 key of the main keyboard.

NUMBER_9.haxe_doc: The 9 key of the main keyboard.

NUMPAD_0.haxe_doc: The 0 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_1.haxe_doc: The 1 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_2.haxe_doc: The 2 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_3.haxe_doc: The 3 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_4.haxe_doc: The 4 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_5.haxe_doc: The 5 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_6.haxe_doc: The 6 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_7.haxe_doc: The 7 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_8.haxe_doc: The 8 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_9.haxe_doc: The 9 key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_MULT.haxe_doc: The `*` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_ADD.haxe_doc: The `+` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_ENTER.haxe_doc: The Enter key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_SUB.haxe_doc: The `-` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_DOT.haxe_doc: The `.` key of the numeric keypad.

NUMPAD_DIV.haxe_doc: The `/` key of the numeric keypad.

MOUSE_WHEEL_UP.haxe_doc: * Mouse wheel does not have an off signal, and should be checked only through `isPressed` method. * Note that there may be multiple wheel scrolls between 2 frames, and to receive more accurate * results, it is recommended to directly listen to wheel events which also provide OS-generated wheel delta value. * See `Interactive.onWheel` for per-interactive events. For scene-based see `Scene.addEventListener` * when event is `EWheel`. For global hook use `Window.addEventTarget` method.

MOUSE_WHEEL_DOWN.haxe_doc: * Mouse wheel does not have an off signal, and should be checked only through `isPressed` method. * Note that there may be multiple wheel scrolls between 2 frames, and to receive more accurate * results, it is recommended to directly listen to wheel events which also provide OS-generated wheel delta value. * See `Interactive.onWheel` for per-interactive events. For scene-based see `Scene.addEventListener` * when event is `EWheel`. For global hook use `Window.addEventTarget` method.

LOC_LEFT.haxe_doc: a bit that is set for left keys

LOC_RIGHT.haxe_doc: a bit that is set for right keys

ALLOW_KEY_REPEAT.haxe_doc: This enable the native key repeat behavior, and will report several times isPressed() in case a key is kept pressed for a long time if this is allowed by the target platform.

isDown.haxe_doc: Tells if the key or mouse button is currently down.

getFrame.haxe_doc: Returns the frame number used to timestamp the key events.

isPressed.haxe_doc: Tells if the key or mouse button was pressed since the last frame.

isReleased.haxe_doc: Tells if the key or mouse button was released since the last frame.

initialize.haxe_doc: Starts listening to the events of the window. Called by `hxd.App`.

dispose.haxe_doc: Stops listening to the events of the window and clears the key states.

getKeyName.haxe_doc: Returns a readable name for the key code, such as `"Escape"` or `"F1"`, or `null` if unknown.

class.haxe_doc: The key codes, and the state of the keyboard and mouse buttons, to poll in the update loop. Mouse buttons use the codes `0` to `6`, so they can be tested with the same functions as keys. For Shift, Ctrl and Alt, both the generic code (`SHIFT`) and the located code (`LSHIFT` or `RSHIFT`) are reported. `hxd.App` calls `initialize` automatically.

PI.haxe_doc: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

EPSILON.haxe_doc: A very small value (`1e-10`), used to compare floats.

EPSILON2.haxe_doc: The square of `EPSILON`, used to compare squared distances.

isFinite.haxe_doc: Tells if `v` is neither infinite nor `NaN`.

fmt.haxe_doc: Rounds `v` to 4 significant digits, and returns `0` for values under `1e-6`. Useful to print values.

exp.haxe_doc: Returns e raised to the power `f`.

logBase.haxe_doc: Returns the logarithm of `f` in the given base.

floor.haxe_doc: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to `f`.

ffloor.haxe_doc: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to `f`, as a `Float`.

ceil.haxe_doc: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to `f`.

round.haxe_doc: Returns `f` rounded to the nearest integer.

fround.haxe_doc: Returns `f` rounded to the nearest integer, as a `Float`.

clamp.haxe_doc: Returns `f` limited to the `[min, max]` range (`[0, 1]` by default).

cos.haxe_doc: Returns the cosine of the angle `f`, in radians.

sin.haxe_doc: Returns the sine of the angle `f`, in radians.

tan.haxe_doc: Returns the tangent of the angle `f`, in radians.

acos.haxe_doc: Returns the arc cosine of `f`, in radians.

asin.haxe_doc: Returns the arc sine of `f`, in radians.

atan.haxe_doc: Returns the arc tangent of `f`, in radians.

atan2.haxe_doc: Returns the angle of the vector `(dx, dy)`, in radians in the `[-PI, PI]` range.

iabs.haxe_doc: Returns the absolute value of the integer `i`.

imax.haxe_doc: Returns the greatest of the integers `a` and `b`.

imin.haxe_doc: Returns the smallest of the integers `a` and `b`.

iclamp.haxe_doc: Returns the integer `v` limited to the `[min, max]` range.

lerp.haxe_doc: Linear interpolation between two values. When k is 0 a is returned, when it's 1, b is returned.

inverseLerp.haxe_doc: Returns a value between 0 and 1, that determines where val lies between a and b.

ease.haxe_doc: Similar to linear interpolation (k is between [0,1]), but can be controled with easing parameter. When easing is 0 it's linear.

lerpTime.haxe_doc: Same as lerp but is scaled based on current FPS, using current elapsed time in seconds.

bitCount.haxe_doc: Returns the number of bits set to 1 in `v`.

isPOT.haxe_doc: Tells if `v` is a power of two (also true for `0`).

nextPOT.haxe_doc: Returns the smallest power of two greater than or equal to `v`.

distanceSq.haxe_doc: Returns the squared length of the vector `(dx, dy, dz)`.

distance.haxe_doc: Returns the length of the vector `(dx, dy, dz)`.

angle.haxe_doc: Wraps an angle into the `]-PI, PI]` range. Can be used to measure the direction between two angles : if Math.angle(A-B) < 0 go left else go right.

angleLerp.haxe_doc: Interpolates from angle `a` to angle `b` by `k`, using the shortest way around the circle.

angleMove.haxe_doc: Move angle a towards angle b with a max increment. Return the new angle.

valueMove.haxe_doc: Move a value towards the given target using the max increment. Return the new value.

shuffle.haxe_doc: Shuffles the array in place, using `Std.random`.

random.haxe_doc: Returns a random float between `0` (included) and `max` (excluded).

srand.haxe_doc: Returns a signed random between -max and max (both included).

b2f.haxe_doc: * takes an int , masks it and devide so that it safely maps 0...255 to 0...1.0 * @paramv an int between 0 and 255 will be masked * @return a float between( 0 and 1)

f2b.haxe_doc: * takes a float , clamps it and multipy so that it safely maps 0...1 to 0...255.0 * @param f a float * @return an int [0...255]

umod.haxe_doc: * returns the modulo but always positive

ufmod.haxe_doc: * returns the modulo but always positive

class.haxe_doc: Math helpers, inlined where possible: most functions call `std.Math`, with `Int` and `Float` variants and game-oriented additions (angles, interpolation, random).

typedef.haxe_doc: The mapping of the buttons and axes of a game pad: each field is the index of the button or axis in `Pad.buttons` and `Pad.values`. `names` gives a display name for each index.

ANALOG_BUTTON_THRESHOLDS.haxe_doc: The values at which an analog input (trigger or axis) is considered as pressed and released in `buttons`.

DEFAULT_CONFIG.haxe_doc: The default configuration for the current platform.

createDummy.haxe_doc: Creates a new dummy unconnected game pad, which can be used instead of checking for null everytime. Use wait() to get real physical game pad access.

wait.haxe_doc: Wait until a gamepad gets connected. On some platforms, this might require the user to press a button until it activates

connected.haxe_doc: Tells if the pad is connected. It is `false` for a dummy pad and after a disconnection.

name.haxe_doc: The name of the pad, as reported by the system.

index.haxe_doc: The index of the pad, or `-1` for a dummy pad.

config.haxe_doc: The mapping of the buttons and axes, used to read `buttons` and `values` by name, as in `pad.isDown(pad.config.A)`.

xAxis.haxe_doc: The X axis of the left stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

yAxis.haxe_doc: The Y axis of the left stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

rxAxis.haxe_doc: The X axis of the right stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

ryAxis.haxe_doc: The Y axis of the right stick, from `-1` to `1`. It is `0` when the stick is inside `axisDeadZone`.

axisDeadZone.haxe_doc: The radius around the center under which the sticks report `0`.

buttons.haxe_doc: The state of each button, indexed as in `config`.

values.haxe_doc: The value of each button (`0` to `1`) or axis (`-1` to `1`), indexed as in `config`.

prevValues.haxe_doc: The values of the previous frame.

onDisconnect.haxe_doc: Called when the pad is disconnected.

isDown.haxe_doc: Tells if the button is down.

isPressed.haxe_doc: Tells if the button was pressed since the previous frame.

isReleased.haxe_doc: Tells if the button was released since the previous frame.

reset.haxe_doc: Resets all buttons and axes to their released state.

rumble.haxe_doc: Makes the pad vibrate with the given `strength` (`0` to `1`) for `time_s` seconds, if supported.

class.haxe_doc: A game pad (controller). Use `Pad.wait` to be notified of connected pads, and read `buttons`, `values` and the axes every frame. `Pad.createDummy` returns an unconnected pad that can be used before a real one is connected.

repeat.haxe_doc: The period of the noise in grid cells along X and Y, to make it tile. No tiling by default.

adjustScale.haxe_doc: Sets `repeat` so that a noise sampled at `x * scale` tiles over `size` units, and returns the corrected scale to use.

gradient3D.haxe_doc: Returns a single octave of 3D noise at the given position.

gradient1D.haxe_doc: Returns a single octave of 1D noise at the given position.

gradient.haxe_doc: Returns a single octave of 2D noise at the given position.

perlin.haxe_doc: Returns fractal 2D noise: the sum of `octaves` layers of `gradient`, each one with its amplitude multiplied by `persist` and its frequency by `lacunarity`. The result is divided by the total amplitude if `normalize` is set.

ridged.haxe_doc: Returns ridged multifractal 2D noise, which produces sharp crests (useful for mountains).

thresholdValue.haxe_doc: Converts a desired probability in the [0,1] range into the corresponding perlin value that we must test against for threshold.

maxValue.haxe_doc: Returns the total amplitude of `octaves` layers with the given `persist`: the maximum absolute value of a non normalized `perlin`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a generator.

class.haxe_doc: Gradient (Perlin) noise generator in 1D, 2D and 3D, with fractal (multi-octave) and ridged variants. Each `seed` gives a different noise. Single octave values are roughly in the `[-1, 1]` range.

ReadOnly.haxe_doc: The bytes are shared and must not be modified: they are copied before the first change.

AlphaPremultiplied.haxe_doc: The colors are premultiplied by the alpha.

enum.haxe_doc: Flags of a `Pixels`.

abstract.haxe_doc: `Pixels` converted to the `ARGB` format, with fast pixel access.

getPixel.haxe_doc: Returns the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

setPixel.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `ARGB` in place.

getPixel.haxe_doc: Returns the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

setPixel.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the pixel, in `0xAARRGGBB` format.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `ARGB` in place.

abstract.haxe_doc: `Pixels` converted to the `R32F` format, with fast pixel access.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the pixel in the X component of `v` (or of a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the pixel to the X component of `v`.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `R32F` in place.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the pixel in the X component of `v` (or of a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the pixel to the X component of `v`.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `R32F` in place.

abstract.haxe_doc: `Pixels` converted to the `RGBA32F` format, with fast pixel access.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the 4 values of the pixel in `v` (or in a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the 4 values of the pixel.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `RGBA32F` in place.

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the 4 values of the pixel in `v` (or in a new vector).

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the 4 values of the pixel.

fromPixels.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to `RGBA32F` in place.

abstract.haxe_doc: A color channel.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the channel.

fromInt.haxe_doc: Returns the channel of the given index.

toInt.haxe_doc: Returns the index of the channel.

fromInt.haxe_doc: Returns the channel of the given index.

switchEndian.haxe_doc: Reverses the order of the 4 bytes of `v`.

switchBR.haxe_doc: Swaps the first and third bytes of `v` (converts between `0xAARRGGBB` and `0xAABBGGRR`).

calcDataSize.haxe_doc: Returns the size in bytes of an image of the given size and format.

calcStride.haxe_doc: Returns the size in bytes of a row of pixels (of a row of 4x4 blocks for compressed formats).

isFloatFormat.haxe_doc: Tells if the format stores float values (16 or 32 bits floats).

getChannelOffset.haxe_doc: Returns the byte offset for the requested channel (0=R,1=G,2=B,3=A) Returns -1 if the channel is not found

alloc.haxe_doc: Allocates an image of the given size and format, filled with zeros.

toDDSLayers.haxe_doc: Build DDS texture bytes from an array of pixels : - can contain a single image - can contain multiple layers (set isCubeMap = true if it's a cubemap) - can contain single or multiple layers with mipmaps (auto detected with diffences in size)

bytes.haxe_doc: The data of the image, starting at `offset`.

format.haxe_doc: The format of the pixels. Use `convert` to change it.

width.haxe_doc: The width in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height in pixels.

dataSize.haxe_doc: The size of the image data in bytes.

offset.haxe_doc: The position of the image data in `bytes`.

sub.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of a rectangle of the image. Throws if it is outside the image.

blit.haxe_doc: Copies a rectangle of `src` at the given position. `src` is converted to the format of this image first.

clear.haxe_doc: Fills the image with the color, in `0xAARRGGBB` format. The bits set in `preserveMask` keep their current value. Only supported for 4 bytes formats (`BGRA`, `RGBA`, `ARGB`), unless all the bytes of the color are equal.

toVector.haxe_doc: Returns the colors of the pixels in `0xAARRGGBB` format. Only supported for `BGRA`, `RGBA` and `ARGB`.

makeSquare.haxe_doc: Extends the image to power of two dimensions, filling the new pixels with zeros. Returns a new image if `copy` is set, or modifies this one.

flipY.haxe_doc: Flips the image vertically, in place.

convert.haxe_doc: Converts the pixels to the `target` format, in place. Throws if the conversion is not supported.

getPixel.haxe_doc: Returns the color of the pixel in `0xAARRGGBB` format (for `BGRA`, `RGBA` and `ARGB`), or its raw value (for `R8` and `RG8`).

setPixel.haxe_doc: Sets the color of the pixel in `0xAARRGGBB` format (for `BGRA`, `RGBA` and `ARGB`), or its raw value (for `R8` and `RG8`).

getPixelF.haxe_doc: Returns the value of the pixel as floats in `v` (or in a new vector). 8 and 16 bits channels are returned in the `[0, 1]` range.

setPixelF.haxe_doc: Sets the value of the pixel from floats. 8 and 16 bits channels take values in the `[0, 1]` range.

dispose.haxe_doc: Releases the bytes of the image.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns a description of the size and format of the image.

toPNG.haxe_doc: Encodes the image as a PNG file with the given compression level. Images not in `ARGB` or `R8` format are converted to `BGRA` first.

toDDS.haxe_doc: Encodes the image as a DDS file (see `toDDSLayers`).

clone.haxe_doc: Returns a copy of the image.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an image using the given bytes, without copying them. See `alloc` to allocate new bytes.

class.haxe_doc: An image in CPU memory: its bytes, size and `PixelFormat`. It is used to load, convert and save images, and to upload data to a `h3d.mat.Texture`.

hash.haxe_doc: Returns a well distributed hash of the integer `n` (Murmur3 mixing), useful as a stateless random value.

create.haxe_doc: Create a randomized hxd.Rand (using a Std.random number as seed)

init.haxe_doc: Initialize the random generator with a seed.

random.haxe_doc: Return a random integer between 0 and n (excluded).

rand.haxe_doc: Return a random float between 0.0 and 1.0 (excluded)

srand.haxe_doc: Return a random float between -scale and +scale (excluded)

new.haxe_doc: Create a random generator with a seed.

class.haxe_doc: `hxd.Rand` is a seeded random number generator, that allows to get always the same results starting from a given seed.

readSaveData.haxe_doc: Override this method to provide custom save lookup. By default it uses `name + ".sav"` for system targets and `localStorage.getItem(name)` on JS. **Note:** This method is an utility method, to load data use `hxd.Save.load`

writeSaveData.haxe_doc: Override this method to provide custom save storage. By default it stores saves in `name + ".sav"` file in current working directory on system targets and `localStorage.setItem(name)` on JS. **Note:** This method is an utility method, to save data use `hxd.Save.save`

delete.haxe_doc: Deletes save with specified name. Override this method when using custom save lookup.

save.haxe_doc: Saves `val` under the specified name. @param checkSum When set, save data is prepended by salted crc checksum for data validation. When save is loaded, `checkSum` flag should be set accordingly.

class.haxe_doc: Save provides simple interface to save and load serialized user data. Data is serialized to String with `haxe.Serializer` and then stored in text form.

enablePhysicalMouse.haxe_doc: * enablePhysicalMouse : enable mouse movements of system mouse, set it to false anse use setMousePos instead to manually set mouse position

mouseCheckMove.haxe_doc: * enable/disable per frame check of elements under mouse (default:true)

defaultCursor.haxe_doc: * Default cursor when there is no Interactive present under cursor.

setMousePos.haxe_doc: Sets the mouse position, used when `enablePhysicalMouse` is disabled.

addScene.haxe_doc: Adds a scene, at the end of the list or at `index`. The scenes receive events in list order.

dispose.haxe_doc: Stops listening to the window events.

focus.haxe_doc: Gives the focus to the interactive, which then receives the key, text and wheel events. The interactive can refuse it by cancelling the `EFocus` event.

blur.haxe_doc: Removes the focus from the current interactive. It can refuse it by cancelling the `EFocusLost` event.

checkEvents.haxe_doc: Dispatches the pending events. Called every frame by `hxd.App`.

startCapture.haxe_doc: Sends all the following events to `f` until `stopCapture` is called, such as for a drag operation. `onCancel` is called when the capture stops. If `touchId` is set, only the events of this touch are captured.

getFocus.haxe_doc: Returns the interactive which has the focus.

updateCursor.haxe_doc: Updates the displayed cursor after the cursor of the interactive changed.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an event dispatcher listening to the window (the current one by default).

class.haxe_doc: Dispatches the window input events to the interactives of one or more scenes. It handles the focus, the over/out events, the mouse capture and the cursor. `hxd.App` creates one as `sevents`, with `s2d` and `s3d` added.

enum.haxe_doc: The kind of platform the application runs on (see `System.platform`).
Boolean system properties, queried with `System.getValue`.
The detected keyboard layout (see `System.getKeyboardLayout`).

class.haxe_doc: Use `sys.io.File.write` to create a `FileOutput`.

wantedFPS.haxe_doc: The FPS on which "tmod" have values are based on. Can be freely configured if your gameplay runs at a different speed. Default : 60

maxDeltaTime.haxe_doc: The maximum amount of time between two frames (in seconds). If the time exceed this amount, Timer will consider these lags are to be ignored. Default : 0.5

smoothFactor.haxe_doc: The smoothing done between frames. A smoothing of 0 gives "real time" values, higher values will smooth the results for tmod/dt/fps over frames using the formula dt = lerp(elapsedTime, dt, smoothFactor) Default : 0 on HashLink, 0.95 on other platforms

lastTimeStamp.haxe_doc: The last timestamp in which update() function was called.

elapsedTime.haxe_doc: The amount of time (unsmoothed) that was spent since the last frame.

frameCount.haxe_doc: A frame counter, increases on each call to update()

tmod.haxe_doc: The smoothed frame modifier, based on wantedFPS. Its value is the same as dt/wantedFPS Allows to express movements in terms of pixels-per-frame-at-wantedFPS instead of per second.

update.haxe_doc: Update the timer calculus on each frame. This is automatically called by hxd.App

skip.haxe_doc: After some loading / long processing, call skip() in order to prevent it from impacting your smoothed values.

reset.haxe_doc: Similar as skip() but also reset dt to default value. Can be used when starting a new game if you want to discard any previous measurement.

class.haxe_doc: The Timer class acts as a global time measurement that can be accessed from various parts of the engine. These three values are representation of the same underlying calculus: tmod, dt, fps

width.haxe_doc: The width of the screen in pixels (of the page on JS: the body width multiplied by the device pixel ratio).

height.haxe_doc: The height of the screen in pixels (of the page on JS: the body height multiplied by the device pixel ratio).

lang.haxe_doc: The language code of the user, such as `"en"`.

platform.haxe_doc: The platform the application runs on.

screenDPI.haxe_doc: The resolution of the screen in dots per inch (currently always `72`).

setCursor.haxe_doc: Sets the current cursor. It can be replaced by a custom function, which should call `setNativeCursor` with the cursor to display.

allowTimeout.haxe_doc: Tells if the infinite loop check is enabled. Set it to `false` to temporarily disable it during long computations.

allowLCID.haxe_doc: If set, `lang` keeps the region code for the locales that need it (such as `"zh-TW"` for traditional Chinese).

getCurrentLoop.haxe_doc: Returns the function called every frame, set with `setLoop`.

setLoop.haxe_doc: Sets the function called every frame by the main loop.

createWindow.haxe_doc: Creates the main window. Its size and title can be set with the `-D windowSize=WIDTHxHEIGHT`, `-D windowTitle=...` and `-D windowFixed=1` defines. Can be replaced to customize the window.

start.haxe_doc: Initializes the system and calls the given function. On HashLink, the window is created with `createWindow` first, and the main loop then runs until the application exits. Called by `hxd.App`.

onReload.haxe_doc: onReload() is called when app hot reload is enabled with -D hot-reload and is also enabled when running hashlink. The later can be done by running `hl --hot-reload` or by setting hotReload:true in VSCode launch props.

reportError.haxe_doc: Called when an uncaught exception occurs in the main loop. By default, writes the error and its call stack to stderr, and on Windows also shows them in a dialog. Can be replaced to log or report errors.

setNativeCursor.haxe_doc: Sets the displayed cursor. Meant to be called by a custom `setCursor`: calling it outside of the automatic interactive cursor update leads to undefined behavior.

getClipboardText.haxe_doc: Returns the text in the system clipboard, or `null` if not supported. On JS, returns the last text set with `setClipboardText`, since the browser clipboard can't be read synchronously.

setClipboardText.haxe_doc: Sets the text in the system clipboard. Returns `false` if not supported.

getDeviceName.haxe_doc: Returns a description of the device, such as `"PC/"` followed by the graphics device name (`"Unknown"` on JS).

getDefaultFrameRate.haxe_doc: Returns the default frame rate of the platform.

getValue.haxe_doc: Returns the value of a system property.

exit.haxe_doc: Exits the application (does nothing on JS).

openURL.haxe_doc: Opens the URL in the default browser (in a new tab on JS).

_loc.haxe_doc: * Returns the locale including region code ()

getLocale.haxe_doc: Returns the locale of the user, including the region code (such as `"en-US"`), based on the system or browser language.

getKeyboardLayout.haxe_doc: Returns the detected keyboard layout, or `Unknown` if it can't be detected (always on JS). The value isn't reliable on SDL without a window.

onKeyboardLayoutChange.haxe_doc: Called when the keyboard layout changes.

timeoutTick.haxe_doc: Notifies the infinite loop check that the application is still running. Call it frequently during long computations, or disable `allowTimeout`.

class.haxe_doc: Platform-specific services: main loop, cursor, clipboard, locale, and screen information. Each target has its own implementation (`System.hl.hx`, `System.js.hx`).

hasEvent.haxe_doc: Tells if there are callbacks waiting.

clear.haxe_doc: Removes all the callbacks.

add.haxe_doc: Adds a callback called every update with the elapsed time; it is removed when it returns `true`.

waitUntil.haxe_doc: Same as `add`: `callb` is called every update until it returns `true`.

update.haxe_doc: Updates the callbacks with the elapsed time `dt`, in seconds.

new.haxe_doc: Creates an empty list.

typedef.haxe_doc: How the window is displayed (see `Window.displayMode`). On HashLink, it is the display mode type of the native library (SDL or DirectX) when one is used.
A monitor, as returned by `Window.getMonitors`.
A display mode of a monitor: resolution and refresh rate.

getMonitors.haxe_doc: Returns the list of the connected monitors.

getInstance.haxe_doc: Returns the current window (on JS, it is created for the `#webgl` canvas if needed).

hasWindow.haxe_doc: Tells if at least one window is open.

id.haxe_doc: The identifier of the native window (only set with the `multidriver` define).

x.haxe_doc: The X position of the window on the screen (of the canvas in the page on JS).

y.haxe_doc: The Y position of the window on the screen (of the canvas in the page on JS).

width.haxe_doc: The width of the drawable area in pixels.

height.haxe_doc: The height of the drawable area in pixels.

mouseX.haxe_doc: The X position of the mouse, relative to the window.

mouseY.haxe_doc: The Y position of the mouse, relative to the window.

mouseLock.haxe_doc: Tells if the mouse is locked. Deprecated: use `mouseMode = AbsoluteUnbound(true)`.

mouseClip.haxe_doc: If set, will restrain the mouse cursor within the window boundaries.

mouseMode.haxe_doc:
Set the mouse movement input handling mode.
@see `hxd.impl.MouseMode` for more details on each mode.

monitor.haxe_doc: The index of the monitor used in fullscreen and borderless modes, or `null` to use the current monitor.

framerate.haxe_doc: The refresh rate to use when changing the resolution in fullscreen mode, or `null` to keep the current one.

vsync.haxe_doc: Tells if the rendering is synchronized with the screen refresh. It can't be disabled on JS.

isFocused.haxe_doc: Tells if the window has the focus.

displayScale.haxe_doc: Get the preferred scaling ratio for high dpi displays for this window

title.haxe_doc: The title of the window (of the page on JS).

displayMode.haxe_doc: The display mode of the window: windowed, borderless or fullscreen. On JS, any mode other than `Windowed` requests the browser fullscreen.

currentMonitorIndex.haxe_doc: The index of the monitor containing the window.

onClose.haxe_doc: Called when the user asks to close the window. Return `false` to keep it open.

onMove.haxe_doc: Called when the window is moved.

onMouseModeChange.haxe_doc: Called when `mouseMode` changes, including when only the parameters of the mode change. Returns a mouse mode to use instead of `to`, or `null` to keep it.

event.haxe_doc: Sends an event to all the event targets.

addEventTarget.haxe_doc: Adds a function called for every input event of the window.

addResizeEvent.haxe_doc: Adds a function called when the window is resized.

resize.haxe_doc: Resizes the window (not supported on JS). In fullscreen mode, it also changes the screen resolution to the closest available one.

setPosition.haxe_doc: Moves the window on the screen (not supported on JS).

addDragAndDropTarget.haxe_doc: Adds a function called when files are dropped on the window.

setCursorPos.haxe_doc: Moves the mouse cursor, relative to the window. If `emitEvent` is set, an `EMove` event is sent. On JS, the browser can't move the cursor: it is only allowed in relative mouse modes, and sets the mouse position.

captureMouseEvents.haxe_doc: Enables or disables the mouse capture: while enabled, the window keeps receiving mouse events when the cursor leaves it.

setFullScreen.haxe_doc: Enables or disables fullscreen mode. Deprecated: use `displayMode`.

setIcon.haxe_doc: Sets the icon of the window (not supported on JS).

isMaximized.haxe_doc: Tells if the window is maximized.

getCurrentDisplaySetting.haxe_doc: Returns the current display setting of the monitor (the first one by default). On DirectX, if `registry` is set, returns the default setting instead of the one changed by the application.

getDisplaySettings.haxe_doc: Returns the display settings available on the monitor (`monitor` by default), keeping only the ones of at least 720 pixels high and 60 Hz (or 30 Hz) when there are any.

setCurrent.haxe_doc: Makes this window the current one, returned by `getInstance`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a window. On HashLink: with the given title and size; flags: `fixed` disables resizing, `hidden` creates it hidden, `background` (DirectX) creates it without activating it. The main window is created by `hxd.System.createWindow`. On JS: for the given canvas, or for the `#webgl` canvas of the page. If `globalEvents` is set (or the canvas has the `globalEvents="1"` attribute), events are captured on the whole page instead of only the canvas.

class.haxe_doc: The application window, which receives the input events and resize notifications. On JS, it is a canvas of the page. Use `Window.getInstance()` to get the current window. Each target has its own implementation (`Window.hl.hx`, `Window.js.hx`).

class.haxe_doc: Ported from https://github.com/mapbox/earcut by @ncannasse

version.haxe_doc: The FBX version that was decoded

keepJoints.haxe_doc: Allows to prevent some terminal unskinned joints to be removed, for instance if we want to track their position

skipObjects.haxe_doc: Allows to skip some objects from being processed as if they were not part of the FBX

fourBonesByVertex.haxe_doc: Use 4 bones of influence per vertex instead of 3

maxBonesPerSkin.haxe_doc: If there are too many bones, the model will be split in separate render passes.

unskinnedJointsAsObjects.haxe_doc: Consider unskinned joints to be simple objects

normalizeScaleOrient.haxe_doc: Convert centimeters to meters and axis to Z-up (Maya FBX export)

highPrecision.haxe_doc: Keep high precision values. Might increase animation data size and compressed size.

legacyScaleAxisConversion.haxe_doc: Use the legacy system to convert scale and axis of FBX file

legacySkinImport.haxe_doc: Use the legacy system to import skinned mesh of FBX file

getAnimationNames.haxe_doc: Returns an array of names with all animations present in FBX file.

getIndexes.haxe_doc: Decode polygon informations into triangle indexes and vertices indexes. Returns vidx, which is the list of vertices indexes and iout which is the index buffer for the full vertex model

name.haxe_doc: The name of the file, with its extension.

path.haxe_doc: The path of the file, relative to the file system root.

directory.haxe_doc: The path of the parent directory.

extension.haxe_doc: The extension of the file name, in lowercase, without the dot.

size.haxe_doc: The size of the file in bytes.

isDirectory.haxe_doc: Tells if the entry is a directory.

isAvailable.haxe_doc: Tells if the content is available. When it is not (files loaded on demand), call `load` first.

getBytes.haxe_doc: Returns the whole content of the file.

readBytes.haxe_doc: Reads `len` bytes at `pos` in the file into `out` at `outPos`, and returns the number of bytes read.

readBytesAsync.haxe_doc: Same as readBytes, but the read is performed in async mode onDone is called in the calling thread (through its event loop) with the number of bytes read, unless the request is cancelled. The out bytes must not be accessed until then.

fetchBytes.haxe_doc: Similar to readBytes except : a) a temporary buffer is reused, meaning a single fetchBytes must occur at a single time b) it will throw an Eof exception if the data is not available

readFull.haxe_doc: Reads `len` bytes at `pos` in the file into `bytes`. Throws `haxe.io.Eof` if fewer bytes are available.

getSign.haxe_doc: Read first 4 bytes of the file.

getText.haxe_doc: Returns the content of the file as text.

open.haxe_doc: Returns an input to read the file.

load.haxe_doc: Makes the content available, then calls `onReady`.

loadBitmap.haxe_doc: Decodes the image file with the platform decoder (asynchronously on JS).

watch.haxe_doc: Calls `onChanged` when the file changes, if the file system supports it. Set `null` to stop watching.

exists.haxe_doc: For a directory, tells if it contains an entry with the given name.

get.haxe_doc: For a directory, returns the entry with the given name.

iterator.haxe_doc: For a directory, iterates over its entries.

class.haxe_doc: A file or directory of a `FileSystem`. Subclasses implement the access for each kind of file system.

addPak.haxe_doc:
Add the .pak file directly.
This method is intended to be used with single-threaded environment such as HTML5 target, as it doesn't have access to sys package.
Use with multi-threaded environment at your own risk.

abstract.haxe_doc: The state of an `AsyncRead`.

Done.haxe_doc: Read, and the callback was called.
Read, and the callback was called.

outPos.haxe_doc: The position in `out` where the data is written.

pos.haxe_doc: The position in the file where the read starts.

len.haxe_doc: The number of bytes to read.

priority.haxe_doc: Requests with higher priority are read first. Can be modified while the request is pending.

bytesRead.haxe_doc: Number of bytes read, once the read is done.

cancel.haxe_doc: Cancel the read : the onDone callback will not be called. If the read was already in progress, the `out` bytes might still be written until it completes.

class.haxe_doc: A pending asynchronous read, returned by `FileEntry.readBytesAsync`. The `out` bytes must not be accessed until the read is done.

ENABLED.haxe_doc: Set to false to emulate all async reads synchronously.

isAsync.haxe_doc: Tells if the reads are really asynchronous (on threaded targets when `ENABLED` is set), or emulated.

read.haxe_doc: Requests the read of `len` bytes at `pos` in the file into `out` at `outPos`. `onDone` is called with the number of bytes read.

promise.haxe_doc: Prevents the requesting thread event loop from terminating while the read is pending.

post.haxe_doc: Runs the callback in the requesting thread event loop and delivers the promise.

class.haxe_doc:
Reads file data asynchronously : a single IO thread is shared by all file systems, reading the pending requests by priority order.
The completion callback is called in the thread that requested the read, through its event loop (the main thread loop is run by heaps, other threads need to have an event loop running).
When async reads are not supported (non-threaded target, or ENABLED=false), the reads are emulated : they are done synchronously at the next event loop of the calling thread, in requests order, and the callbacks are called the same way.

class.haxe_doc: A file entry whose content is in memory.

sourceExts.haxe_doc: The extensions of the files this conversion accepts, or `null` for any file.

destExt.haxe_doc: The extension of the converted files, which also identifies the conversion in the rules.

params.haxe_doc: The parameters of the conversion, set by the rule.

localParams.haxe_doc: The parameters computed from the file content by `computeLocalParams`.

dstPath.haxe_doc: The path of the converted file to write.

baseDir.haxe_doc: The root directory of the resources.

originalFilename.haxe_doc: The path of the original resource file, relative to `baseDir`.

srcBytes.haxe_doc: The content of the file to convert, read on demand.

hash.haxe_doc: The calculated hash for the input source file content.

cleanup.haxe_doc: Clears the state of the conversion after it ran.

convert.haxe_doc: Converts `srcPath` and writes the result to `dstPath`.

hasLocalParams.haxe_doc: A function that should return quickly if the convert might have local params or not. Do not have access to: srcBytes, hash.

getLocalContext.haxe_doc: Context will be cached and passed to computeLocalParams next time if file hash has not changed. This function will be called after each call to computeLocalParams for refresh the cache.

computeLocalParams.haxe_doc: Returns the parameters that depend on the file content (see `hasLocalParams` and `getLocalContext`).

new.haxe_doc: Creates a conversion from the comma separated `sourceExts` (`null` for any) to `destExt`.

new.haxe_doc: Creates the conversion.

Converts images to compressed DDS textures with the `texconv` or `CompressonatorCLI` commands. Parameters: `format` (required, such as `BC1`, `BC3` or `RGBA`), `mips`, `size` (maximum size), `alpha` (BC1 alpha threshold).

create.haxe_doc: Converts and embeds all the files of the resource directory, and returns a file system to access them.

dispose.haxe_doc: Does nothing.

dir.haxe_doc: Returns the entries of the directory, sorted by name.

class.haxe_doc: A read-only file system whose files are embedded in the application as Haxe resources. Created with `create`, used by `hxd.Res.initEmbed`.

lock.haxe_doc: Runs `f` while holding the lock (without lock if `heaps_mt_loader` is not set), and returns its result.

class.haxe_doc: A global lock protecting the resource loading when the `heaps_mt_loader` define is set, to load resources from several threads.

rules.haxe_doc: The conversion rules, sorted by priority.

configuration.haxe_doc: The name of the configuration selecting the `fs.convert.<configuration>` rules.

A rule maps a pattern to the destination extension of a `Convert`, such as `"fbx": "hmd"`, or `"png": { "convert": "dds", "format": "BC3" }`. Rules from `fs.convert.<configuration>` override the default ones.

position.haxe_doc: The position of the next byte to read in the file.

insideIncircle.haxe_doc:
* Requirement:
* 1. a, b and c form a triangle.
* 2. a and d is know to be on opposite side of bc
* 
	 *                a
	 *                +
	 *               / \
	 *              /   \
	 *            b/     \c
	 *            +-------+
	 *           /    d    \
	 *          /           \
	 *
* Fact: d has to be in area B to have a chance to be inside the circle formed by * a,b and c
* d is outside B if orient2d(a,b,d) or orient2d(c,a,d) is CW
* This preknowledge gives us a way to optimize the incircle test * @param pa - triangle point, opposite d * @param pb - triangle point * @param pc - triangle point * @param pd - point opposite a * @return true if d is inside circle, false if on circle edge

abstract.haxe_doc: Options of the meshoptimizer simplification functions.

LockBorder.haxe_doc: Do not move vertices that are located on the topological border (vertices on triangle edges that don't have a paired triangle). Useful for simplifying portions of the larger mesh.

Sparse.haxe_doc: Improve simplification performance assuming input indices are a sparse subset of the mesh. Note that error becomes relative to subset extents.

ErrorAbsolute.haxe_doc: Treat error limit and resulting error as absolute instead of relative to mesh extents.

Prune.haxe_doc: Remove disconnected parts of the mesh during simplification incrementally, regardless of the topological restrictions inside components.

LockBorder.haxe_doc: Do not move vertices that are located on the topological border (vertices on triangle edges that don't have a paired triangle). Useful for simplifying portions of the larger mesh.

Sparse.haxe_doc: Improve simplification performance assuming input indices are a sparse subset of the mesh. Note that error becomes relative to subset extents.

ErrorAbsolute.haxe_doc: Treat error limit and resulting error as absolute instead of relative to mesh extents.

Prune.haxe_doc: Remove disconnected parts of the mesh during simplification incrementally, regardless of the topological restrictions inside components.

abstract.haxe_doc: Options of the meshoptimizer tangent generation.

TangentCompatible.haxe_doc: Produce tangents compatible with MikkTSpace (same weighting and fallbacks) at the cost of reduced quality. Not recommended unless normal maps are baked.

TangentZeroFallback.haxe_doc: Experimental: For vertices only connected to degenerate triangles, output zero tangents instead of an arbitrary fallback.

TangentCompatible.haxe_doc: Produce tangents compatible with MikkTSpace (same weighting and fallbacks) at the cost of reduced quality. Not recommended unless normal maps are baked.

TangentZeroFallback.haxe_doc: Experimental: For vertices only connected to degenerate triangles, output zero tangents instead of an arbitrary fallback.

generateVertexRemap.haxe_doc:
Generates a vertex remap table from the vertex buffer and an optional index buffer and returns number of unique vertices As a result, all vertices that are binary equivalent map to the same (new) location, with no gaps in the resulting sequence. Resulting remap table maps old vertices to new vertices and can be used in remapVertexBuffer/remapIndexBuffer. Note that binary equivalence considers all vertexSize bytes, including padding which should be zero-initialized.
remapOut must contain enough space for the resulting remap table (vertexCount elements) indices can be null if the input is unindexed

remapIndexBuffer.haxe_doc:
Generate index buffer from the source index buffer and remap table generated by generateVertexRemap
indicesOut must contain enough space for the resulting index buffer (indexCount elements) indicesIn can be null if the input is unindexed

remapVertexBuffer.haxe_doc:
Generates vertex buffer from the source vertex buffer and remap table generated by generateVertexRemap
vertexOut must contain enough space for the resulting vertex buffer (vertexCount elements, returned by generateVertexRemap) vertexCount should be the initial vertex count and not the value returned by generateVertexRemap

simplify.haxe_doc:
Mesh simplifier Reduces the number of triangles in the mesh, attempting to preserve mesh appearance as much as possible The algorithm tries to preserve mesh topology and can stop short of the target goal based on topology constraints or target error. If not all attributes from the input mesh are required, it's recommended to reindex the mesh without them prior to simplification. Returns the number of indices after simplification, with destination containing new index data The resulting index buffer references vertices from the original vertex buffer. If the original vertex data isn't required, creating a compact vertex buffer using optimizeVertexFetch is recommended.
indicesOut must contain enough space for the target index buffer, worst case is indexCount elements (*not* targetIndexCount)! vertices should have float3 position in the first 12 bytes of each vertex targetError represents the error relative to mesh extents that can be tolerated, e.g. 0.01 = 1% deformation; value range [0..1] options must be a bitmask composed of meshopt_SimplifyX options; 0 is a safe default resultErrorOut can be null; when it's not null, it will contain the resulting (relative) error after simplification

optimizeVertexCache.haxe_doc:
Vertex transform cache optimizer Reorders indices to reduce the number of GPU vertex shader invocations If index buffer contains multiple ranges for multiple draw calls, this functions needs to be called on each range individually.
indicesOut must contain enough space for the resulting index buffer (indexCount elements)

optimizeOverdraw.haxe_doc:
Overdraw optimizer Reorders indices to reduce the number of GPU vertex shader invocations and the pixel overdraw If index buffer contains multiple ranges for multiple draw calls, this functions needs to be called on each range individually.
indicesOut must contain enough space for the resulting index buffer (indexCount elements) indicesIn must contain index data that is the result of optimizeVertexCache (*not* the original mesh indices!) vertices should have float3 position in the first 12 bytes of each vertex threshold indicates how much the overdraw optimizer can degrade vertex cache efficiency (1.05 = up to 5%) to reduce overdraw more efficiently

optimizeVertexFetch.haxe_doc:
Vertex fetch cache optimizer Reorders vertices and changes indices to reduce the amount of GPU memory fetches during vertex processing Returns the number of unique vertices, which is the same as input vertex count unless some vertices are unused
verticesOut must contain enough space for the resulting vertex buffer (vertexCount elements) indices is used both as an input and as an output index buffer

getContent.haxe_doc:
Retrieves the content of the file specified by `path` as a String.
If the file does not exist or can not be read, an exception is thrown.
`sys.FileSystem.exists` can be used to check for existence.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

getBytes.haxe_doc:
Retrieves the binary content of the file specified by `path`.
If the file does not exist or can not be read, an exception is thrown.
`sys.FileSystem.exists` can be used to check for existence.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

saveContent.haxe_doc:
Stores `content` in the file specified by `path`.
If the file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
If `path` or `content` are null, the result is unspecified.

saveBytes.haxe_doc:
Stores `bytes` in the file specified by `path` in binary mode.
If the file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
If `path` or `bytes` are null, the result is unspecified.

read.haxe_doc:
Returns an `FileInput` handle to the file specified by `path`.
If `binary` is true, the file is opened in binary mode. Otherwise it is opened in non-binary mode.
If the file does not exist or can not be read, an exception is thrown.
Operations on the returned `FileInput` handle read on the opened file.
File handles should be closed via `FileInput.close` once the operation is complete.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

write.haxe_doc:
Returns an `FileOutput` handle to the file specified by `path`.
If `binary` is true, the file is opened in binary mode. Otherwise it is opened in non-binary mode.
If the file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
Operations on the returned `FileOutput` handle write to the opened file. If the file existed, its previous content is overwritten.
File handles should be closed via `FileOutput.close` once the operation is complete.
If `path` is null, the result is unspecified.

copy.haxe_doc:
Copies the contents of the file specified by `srcPath` to the file specified by `dstPath`.
If the `srcPath` does not exist or cannot be read, or if the `dstPath` file cannot be written to, an exception is thrown.
If the file at `dstPath` exists, its contents are overwritten.
If `srcPath` or `dstPath` are null, the result is unspecified.

class.haxe_doc:
API for reading and writing files.
See `sys.FileSystem` for the complementary file system API.
Use `sys.io.File.read` to create a `FileInput`.

stdout.haxe_doc: Standard output. The output stream where a process writes its output data.

stderr.haxe_doc: Standard error. The output stream to output error messages or diagnostics.

stdin.haxe_doc: Standard input. The stream data going into a process.

exitCode.haxe_doc: Query the exit code of the process. If `block` is true or not specified, it will block until the process terminates. If `block` is false, it will return either the process exit code if it's already terminated or null if it's still running. If the process has already exited, return the exit code immediately.

new.haxe_doc:
Construct a `Process` object, which run the given command immediately.
Command arguments can be passed in two ways: 1. using `args`, 2. appending to `cmd` and leaving `args` as `null`.
1. When using `args` to pass command arguments, each argument will be automatically quoted, and shell meta-characters will be escaped if needed. `cmd` should be an executable name that can be located in the `PATH` environment variable, or a path to an executable.
2. When `args` is not given or is `null`, command arguments can be appended to `cmd`. No automatic quoting/escaping will be performed. `cmd` should be formatted exactly as it would be when typed at the command line. It can run executables, as well as shell commands that are not executables (e.g. on Windows: `dir`, `cd`, `echo` etc).
`detached` allows the created process to be standalone. You cannot communicate with it but you can look at its exit code. Not supported on php.
`close()` should be called when the `Process` is no longer used.

ip.haxe_doc: The actual IP corresponding to the host.

toString.haxe_doc: Returns the IP representation of the host

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new Host : the name can be an IP in the form "127.0.0.1" or an host name such as "google.com", in which case the corresponding IP address is resolved using DNS. An exception occur if the host name could not be found.

class.haxe_doc: A given IP host name.

add.haxe_doc:
Adds an element at the end of `this` Deque.
(Java,Jvm): throws `java.lang.NullPointerException` if `i` is `null`.

push.haxe_doc:
Adds an element at the front of `this` Deque.
(Java,Jvm): throws `java.lang.NullPointerException` if `i` is `null`.

pop.haxe_doc:
Tries to retrieve an element from the front of `this` Deque.
If an element is available, it is removed from the queue and returned.
If no element is available and `block` is `false`, `null` is returned.
Otherwise, execution blocks until an element is available and returns it.

new.haxe_doc: Create a new Deque instance which is initially empty.

class.haxe_doc: A Deque is a double-ended queue with a `pop` method that can block until an element is available. It is commonly used to synchronize threads.

Now.haxe_doc: There's already an event waiting to be executed

AnyTime.haxe_doc: An event is expected to arrive at any time. If `time` is specified, then the event will be ready at that time for sure.

At.haxe_doc: An event is expected to be ready for execution at `time`.

enum.haxe_doc: When an event loop has an available event to execute.

wait.haxe_doc: Waits for the lock to be released, or `timeout` (in seconds) to expire. Returns `true` if the lock is released and `false` if a time-out occurs.

release.haxe_doc:
Releases the lock once.
The thread does not need to own the lock in order to release it. Each call to `release` allows exactly one call to `wait` to execute.

new.haxe_doc: Creates a new Lock which is initially locked.

new.haxe_doc: Creates thread local storage. This is placeholder that can store a value that will be different depending on the local thread. Set the tls value to `null` before exiting the thread or the memory will never be collected.

class.haxe_doc:
Creates thread local storage.
(hl) Warning: At the moment `Tls` does not protect the value from being garbage collected. Keep the value reachable to avoid crashes.
